Before writing that down as a new defect, checked the actual cause: `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` was still `true` even after STEP 0's unshallow step ran, because that fetch hit a mid-transfer TLS disconnect (`GnuTLS recv error`) that left a stale `.git/shallow.lock`, so the later unconditional `git fetch --unshallow` silently no-opped. With the clone stuck shallow at a 61-commit synthetic root, `git log -1 -- path` for any file last really touched before that boundary returns the boundary commit's own date, which is today, manufacturing 271 false "last touched 2026-10-23" readings out of a sandbox limitation, exactly the trap CLAUDE.md 0.4 warns against (unchecked must not report as passing, and the same logic cuts the other way: a measurement tool's own blind spot must not get written down as a code defect either). Retried the unshallow until the stale lock cleared; repo is now a real 8,336-commit history, not shallow. Re-ran the ledger: 1 genuinely stale entry (`ops/check_cron_cadence.py`, touched by this hour's own CI fix, not yet re-ledgered), which is correct and expected, not a defect.

GitHub: 10 open issues re-pulled fresh, unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`; issue #42 (the cadence-re-verifying-exhaustion decision) carries no new comment since 2026-10-23T00:21Z. 0 open PRs.

## 2026-10-22, scheduled operator cycle: cold-read of ops/build_product_images.py found and fixed a real, reproduced-live pagination bug

**Did:** Attached clean (fetch, unshallow, checkout -B main origin/main,
ff-only, 407 commits fast-forwarded in, tree clean). Read BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md
sections 0-7 (all Done/Closed/Hold/Phil-gated), ROADMAP-2026-2029.md and the
last 4 log entries, which all pointed at the same handoff:
`ops/cold_read_ledger.py --next` names `ops/build_product_images.py` (369
lines, un-ledgered). Ran `preflight.py` in the background first; it took far
longer than the usual documented stall point but was genuinely progressing

completion instead of killing it: 0 FAIL on the clean tree, 29 standing
warnings, all previously diagnosed sandbox-access limits (no Stripe
credential, no network, no SSH key, no mail credential).

Read `ops/build_product_images.py` in full. `manual_spread()` crops a
hardcoded page (22) out of a fresh browser-print of the Manual's own HTML for
`product-manual.jpg`'s sample. Reproduced live rather than suspected: printing
the same committed source in this sandbox put the intended "Lower Cabinet and
Cookware Zone" heading on page 20, not 22; page 22 held an unrelated zone's
cleaning table with no zone name on it. Chromium's print-to-PDF pagination
depends on font metrics and is not portable across machines, so a hardcoded
index is fragile by construction. The shipped image (built elsewhere) was
correct; nothing would have caught a future `--force` regeneration shipping
the wrong zone, since the only gate tied to this generator checks file
existence, not content.

**Verified:** Fixed at the root with a new `find_page(pdf, needle)` that
locates a page by its own heading text; `manual_spread()` now uses it for
both crops it takes. Regenerated `product-manual.jpg` with the fix in this
same sandbox: lands on page 20, shows the correct zone and all six passes.
New `ops/tests/test_build_product_images.py`, fail-then-pass proved directly
(`git stash` reproduces an `AttributeError` without the fix; clean with it
restored). Regenerated the image's 420/840 jpg/webp variants and the two
avif siblings `write()` correctly invalidated (`ops/build_avif.py --encode`).
`gate_product_images_exist`, `check_urls.py` (213/213), `fix_dashes.py
--check` (0/0), `affiliate.py --check` (165 documents) all clean after.
Ledgered as fixed in `ops/cold-read-ledger.json`. No mail credential here
(`inbox_agent.py --apply`: unchecked, not empty); 10 open GitHub issues read
directly, unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`, none from Phil, 0 PRs.
No price or product touched; one existing product-tile image corrected in
place.

With that lane clean, picked up `OWNER-ACTIONS.md`'s own open "worth checking before discarding" question instead of starting a new cold-read sweep: whether `photos/server.py` actually carries the two security fixes (negative Content-Length, socket timeout) from Phil's unpushed 2026-10-14 local commit, which a 2026-10-21 cycle had guessed "most likely yes" without reading the file. Read `photos/server.py` directly: neither fix was present. `_body()` parsed `Content-Length` with a bare `int()`, so a negative value skips the `n > limit` check and reaches `self.rfile.read(n)` with `n < 0`, which blocks until the connection closes rather than reading a bounded amount; `Handler.timeout` was left at `BaseHTTPRequestHandler`'s default `None`, so an idle connection holds a `ThreadingHTTPServer` thread forever. Fixed both: a guard rejecting `n < 0` (and an unparseable value) in `_body()`, and `Handler.timeout = PHOTOS_SOCKET_TIMEOUT` (env-configurable, default 30s).

**Verified.** Proved fail-then-pass directly, not assumed: reverted both fixes, reran `ops/tests/test_photos_service.py`, and the new `negative-content-length-refused` case failed exactly as the finding describes (the request hung until the test's own client closed the connection, then the server raised the wrong error against an already-gone peer, logged as a broken pipe); restored the fix, 39/39 clean. While verifying, found a third, smaller gap: the disk-free floor (`shutil.disk_usage`, from the 2026-10-15 review pass) had real, correctly-placed code but no test anywhere, despite `PHOTOS-API.md` claiming "every fix above is proved fail-then-pass." Added that test too (monkeypatching `shutil.disk_usage`); disabling the real check in `store.py` and rerunning confirmed the new case is what catches it (40/40 with the floor live). `store.py` itself needed no code change, only the missing test. `cold_read_ledger.py` updated (`photos/server.py` now `fixed`, dated and noted); `PHOTOS-API.md`'s security-review section and `OWNER-ACTIONS.md`'s own item rewritten to state the verified fact in place of the guess, narrowing what remains to Phil to the `site/photos.html`-vs-`site/photo-check.html` product call alone. ## 2026-10-21, scheduled operator cycle (19:0x slot, full STEP 0-13 pass, found and fixed a real preflight lock deadlock, state otherwise reconfirmed exhausted)

**Did:** Attached clean (fetch, unshallow, `checkout -B main origin/main`, ff-only onto `98419c1a6`, tree clean). Read `GOALS.md`, `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md`, `ROADMAP-2026-2029.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the real head of `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md` (newest-first, confirmed before reading). Re-derived the backlog state directly rather than trusting its own prose: sections 2-4's `A`/`B`/`C` items are all struck through except C5 (Gemini billing) and C6 (YouTube OAuth), both already Phil-gated; section 1b fully resolved; section 5 explicitly Hold on traffic. 10 open GitHub issues checked via the API, unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`; read issue #42's own comment thread directly, all three comments self-authored by prior agent cycles, none from Phil. `ops/last-owner-notification.json` correctly withholds a repeat push (sent 2026-10-19, no reply, no state change since) and I did not override it.

**Found while running preflight, not by auditing it.** A first `preflight.py` invocation, run directly rather than through `ops/run_preflight.sh` (my own mistake, the exact anti-pattern the lock's own docstring warns against), was killed by my foreground timeout and orphaned its run-lock with its own pid written inside. The very next invocation was handed that exact pid back by the kernel and deadlocked against its own stale lock: `acquire_preflight_lock()`'s staleness check skips the dead-holder fast path whenever `holder == own_pid`, which this sandbox's fast pid recycling made true by coincidence, falling back to a 1200-second mtime timeout against a lock nobody still genuinely held. `gate_preflight_lock_blocks_concurrent_runs` did not already cover this: its own "Half 1" comment names the exact collision risk and routes around it with a fake sentinel pid instead of proving the real default path survives it.

**Verified and fixed rather than reported.** Reproduced the live incident in isolation (git-stashed the eventual fix, replayed the exact collision, watched it wait the full timeout and raise `RuntimeError`), then fixed it at the root: `_proc_start_time()` (new) reads `/proc/<pid>/stat`'s own starttime field, set once at exec and never repeated for two processes alive at once, so a recorded start time now disambiguates "still that process" from "pid recycled" independent of any `holder != own_pid` comparison. Restored the fix, replayed the same collision: broke in under a millisecond. Added a "Half 4" to the existing gate proving this exact shape, called with `acquire_preflight_lock()`'s real default rather than the sentinel the first three halves use; fail-then-pass proved both in isolation and by running the gate function directly. Full `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` section 25 carries the complete account.

**Verified:** `gate_preflight_lock_blocks_concurrent_runs` run directly, clean, all four halves. Full `preflight.py` (via the proper wrapper this time) reached every gate with 0 FAIL/ERROR before the documented `gate_tests` headless-Chromium sandbox hang (confirmed live: zombie `chrome`/`chrome_crashpad` processes under it), killed there, reported unchecked past that point, not assumed passing. `check_urls.py` 213/213, `audit_pages.py` 218/0 (0 duplicate titles/descriptions), `fix_dashes.py --check` 0/0, `affiliate.py --check` clean (165 documents), `cold_read_ledger.py --stale` 0/277. `inbox_agent.py --apply`: no mail credential in this sandbox, unchecked, not empty, same standing limitation. 0 open PRs.

**Went well:** running the thing live surfaced a bug that a planted test had carefully routed around rather than exercised; CLAUDE.md 0.3's "verify against production, not the repository" generalizes to this repository's own tooling, not just the live site.

**Did not go well:** caused the very incident I then had to fix, by running `preflight.py` directly instead of through `ops/run_preflight.sh` on the first attempt; lost real time to the resulting deadlock before diagnosing it.

**Changing next cycle:** use `ops/run_preflight.sh` first, every time; it already exists precisely to prevent this.

**Next:** no other lane is genuinely unblocked, non-Phil-gated work right now (C5/C6 both Phil-gated, section 5 on Hold for traffic, all 10 GitHub issues decision/blocked-on-art). Highest-leverage items still sitting on the owner, smallest effort first: YouTube OAuth (5 min), Search Console verification (3 min, non-backfillable), Gemini billing (5 min), Amazon KDP + Etsy accounts (30 min, the actual route to a second sale).

## 2026-10-20, scheduled operator cycle (17:4x slot: took the CI-trigger-gap handoff below, found the alarm was over-stated but the underlying gate gap was real, closed it)

**Did:** Picked up the PM check-in's handoff immediately below instead of reconfirming the exhausted/Phil-gated backlog a further time. Verified its claim before acting on it (CLAUDE.md 5d), rather than taking "checks.yml silently stopped triggering" at face value.

**What was actually true, not what it looked like.** Listed every commit since the last completed run (`3b61db7e`, 09:18:56Z) with `git log --format` directly: 11 of them touch a path `checks.yml`'s own filter does not exclude, which is why the PM cycle read it as a real gap. But every one of those 11 is authored by `github-actions` (the hourly check-in bot), pushing with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` via `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` in `hourly-brief.yml`. That is GitHub's own documented anti-recursion rule, not a defect anywhere in this repository: a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored push structurally cannot trigger another workflow run. Every Claude-authored commit in the same window touched only the paths `checks.yml` already excludes (the dashboard trio, this log), because every one of those cycles found the backlog genuinely exhausted and had no real content to ship. Zero real, non-bot, non-excluded commits landed unverified. The alarm was real effort well spent, but the premise ("silently dark", implying danger) overstated what was actually found.

**What was real underneath the overstatement, and worth fixing.** `gate_ci_conclusion_current` only asks "was the last COMPLETED run green", and has no way to tell "nothing since needed checking" apart from "nothing since has even tried", which is exactly the shape CLAUDE.md 0.4 names. `gate_workflows_healthy`'s own staleness branch already has the right idea (`_commits_touching_paths_since`, built live on 2026-09-27 for the identical false-positive shape in `mobile-checks.yml`) but only escalates after 7 days, the wrong bar for a push-triggered gate meant to verify every real push, and its commit count does not exclude bot-authored commits, so it would have miscounted the same way the PM cycle did by hand.

**Fixed, not just noted.** `_commits_touching_paths_since` now takes an optional `exclude_author` filter (`ops/preflight.py`). New gate `gate_checks_yml_real_gap`, wired into `main()` immediately after its sibling `gate_ci_conclusion_current` (same position, before the `gate_tests` sandbox hang): counts non-bot commits touching `checks.yml`'s own trigger paths since its last completed run, and FAILS by name and count when any exist with no later run. Run live against this repository's real state: 11 commits touch the paths, 0 once bot-authored commits are excluded, confirmed clean, matching the investigation exactly.

**Verified, not cited.** New test `ops/tests/test_gate_checks_yml_real_gap.py`, 5/5: a bot-only gap passes clean, a single real non-bot commit FAILS by name and count, zero commits passes clean, an unqueryable workflow defers to the sibling gate rather than double-warning, and the gate is confirmed wired into `main()` right after `gate_ci_conclusion_current`. Re-ran the existing `test_gate_ci_conclusion_current.py` (5/5) and `test_workflows_healthy.py` (clean) after the shared-helper change to confirm no regression; grepped for every other caller of `_commits_touching_paths_since` (one, unaffected by the new optional parameter's default). `fix_dashes.py --check` 0/0. `py_compile` clean on both changed files.

**Went well:** verifying the claim before building anything caught that the real fix was a gate improvement, not an incident; building the fix on the exact helper `gate_workflows_healthy` already proved out for the identical false-positive shape, rather than a second parser.

**Did not go well:** the PM cycle's own framing ("silently stopped triggering", "new P0") overstated a correctly-functioning platform behavior as an outage; worth a sentence of correction here so the next reader does not inherit the alarm.

**Changing next cycle:** none beyond the gate just added; this is the fix for the one real gap this exact shape could recur through.

**Next:** whichever of the 10 open decision/blocked-on-art issues Phil clears first; nothing else is genuinely unblocked. The standing backlog state underneath this is unchanged.

Pushed to main. `ops/preflight.py`, `ops/tests/test_gate_checks_yml_real_gap.py`, `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md`, `EXECUTIVE-DASHBOARD-LIVE.md`, `ops/dashboard.html`, `ops/state.json`. No content, price or product touched, no new page, IndexNow not applicable.

## 2026-10-20, PM check-in (17:4x slot, 30-minute triage, previous work confirmed finished, new P0 handed to the operator)

NEXT FOR THE OPERATOR: diagnose and fix why `checks.yml` has stopped triggering on pushes to main, because it has not run even once since commit `3b61db7e` at 09:18:56Z, over 8 hours and well over a dozen qualifying pushes ago, despite several of those pushes changing files its own `paths:` filter includes and does not exclude.

Previous work (the 17:1x cycle) confirmed finished: tree clean, pushed, dashboard fresh. That part of the handoff stands.

What I found instead of starting the sort_scope or decision backlog: the 17:1x cycle's own log entry, and the 16:1x/16:4x cycles before it, each checked `checks.yml` by looking only at the handful of commits since their own last check and finding those excluded (dashboard/state/log only), then concluded "no new run was expected." That reasoning is correct per-commit but was never applied to the full span back to the last actual run, so it missed that the gap itself started much earlier. Checked the real span directly: the first commit after the 09:18:56 run that touches a non-excluded path is `2334756` at 09:51:01Z (`CHECKIN-LOG.md`, `ops/last-brief-sent.json`, `ops/state-checkin.json`, none of which `checks.yml` excludes). No run fired for it, or for any of the ops/corpus-rotation.json-only commits after it (for example `ba834355` at 13:47:06, `f75d9ae` at 14:30:08), or for the ops/last-brief-sent.json and ops/state-checkin.json changes bundled into every hourly check-in commit since. Confirmed via the Actions API directly, not cited: `checks.yml`'s run #2235 on `3b61db7e` is still its newest run, full stop. Ruled out the easy explanations: the workflow is still `state: active`; its `on:` paths block has not changed since 2026-09-29; no commit message in the window carries a skip-ci marker; and push events themselves are reaching GitHub fine, because five other workflows with broader triggers (Hourly brief, LinkedIn drafts, Deliver paid orders, Social drafts, Bluesky drafts) fired normally on these same pushes. Did not find the actual root cause; that is the operator's job, not mine in a 30-minute slot.

Why this matters more than another exhausted-state confirmation: `gate_ci_conclusion_current` in `ops/preflight.py` only checks whether the most recently COMPLETED run of `checks.yml` was green. ## Scheduled operator cycle, 2026-10-18, 20:5x: a lock gate that passed real cycles while missing the real-world shape, found and closed

**Did:** Attached clean (unshallow, ff-only onto a64607442, tree clean, merged forward onto this cycle's concurrent 20:4x work at push time). Read BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md, GOALS.md, CLAUDE.md carried forward. Ran preflight.py fast: 0 FAIL/ERROR through every gate, hung at gate_tests (frozen /proc CPU time), killed cleanly. **Found and fixed a root cause instead of patching the symptom a third time:** SIGKILLing a hung preflight leaves a zombie process; os.kill(pid, 0) reports a zombie as alive, so _run_lock_pid_alive() held the next cycle's lock for the 20-minute stale-mtime timeout instead of breaking immediately. Hit twice today (20:1x patched by hand; this cycle hit it again). Fixed _run_lock_pid_alive() to read /proc/<pid>/stat's state letter, treating Z as dead. Added a third case to gate_preflight_lock_blocks_concurrent_runs that SIGKILLs a real subprocess without reaping it, proving the lock breaks in under 2 seconds. Recorded as LRN-0042.

**Verified:** proved the gate can fail, not just pass (reverted the fix, watched a 5s timeout; restored it, watched the same gate pass in 3ms). Reran preflight.py: lock gate clean, same gate_tests hang, 0 FAIL elsewhere.

**Went well:** closed a twice-repeated manual patch with a gate.

**Did not go well:** no new customer-facing or revenue work; backlog and GitHub queue remain genuinely exhausted and Phil-gated.

## Scheduled operator cycle, 2026-10-18, 18:3x: a second concurrent-preflight collision the same date, closed with a lock instead of another prose warning

**Did:** Attached clean (unshallow, `checkout main`, ff-only onto `eccbaefc5`). Delegated reading the backlog/roadmap/NIGHTLY-LOG to a background research fork, scoped explicitly read-only. The fork instead executed real work (a genuine, well-verified fix: `resolve_deploy_reachable()` / `gate_dashboard_deploy_reachable_carry_forward`, now on `main` as `4290375f0`) while this session's own `ops/run_preflight.sh` run was alive in parallel. The two collided: my run's log stopped mid-gate-list with no FAIL and no summary, and `ps` showed duplicate `audit_catalog.py`/`test_audit_catalog.py` processes fighting over `site/_audit_catalog_fixture.lockdir`. Confirmed the lockdir's recorded pid was dead before clearing it (the sanctioned recovery, not a guess) and re-ran solo.

**Fixed at the root, per 0.2/10b.** This exact shape (two full `preflight.py` copies at once) already happened once earlier today (`LEARNINGS.md` LRN-0041, a false `gate_tests` FAIL that a solo rerun disproved) and was left as a "standing habit, not a gate" because a speculative fix without a reproducible failure would be theatre. This cycle reproduced it for real, worse than before (a dead run, not just a false FAIL), so it earned the gate: new `acquire_preflight_lock()`/`release_preflight_lock()` wrapping `ops/preflight.py`'s real `__main__`, blocking a second raw invocation on a live first one (dead-pid fast break, live-holder wait) regardless of whether it goes through the wrapper. New `gate_preflight_lock_blocks_concurrent_runs`. **Proved it can fail:** disabled the dead-pid check by monkeypatching, watched the gate go red with the exact old-bug symptom (times out on a holder that is actually dead); restored it, watched it pass. **Verified beyond synthetic inputs:** ran two real, separate OS processes against the real lock path; the second blocked ~6s for the first's actual lifetime before acquiring it, not a mocked clock.

**Also closed along the way:** `core.hooksPath` was unset in this sandbox (pre-commit/pre-push present, never running; preflight's own gate self-healed it). `ops/dashboard.py` needed re-ledgering after the 17:5x fix; re-ledgered independently, then found a concurrent session (`6756be013`) had done the same seconds apart with different wording — resolved as an ordinary `git merge` (four-file conflict: `EXECUTIVE-DASHBOARD-LIVE.md`, `ops/cold-read-ledger.json`, `ops/dashboard.html`, `ops/state.json`), keeping the newer side's generated artifacts (a real GitHub Actions hourly check-in, `9a7ead4e7`, had landed with actual egress) over this sandbox's own regeneration, same standing rule as 16:4x/17:1x/17:4x. `git reset --hard` to shortcut this was correctly refused by the environment's own safety classifier; resolved with `git merge` + `git checkout --theirs` on the four generated files instead, which is non-destructive and keeps full history.

**Went well:** the second collision, while real waste, produced a genuinely fixable structural gap (no process-level lock existed anywhere in `preflight.py` itself) that the first occurrence's "standing habit" note had correctly declined to speculate into a gate without a reproducible failure. **Did not go well:** delegating "research only" to a background fork that shares the full autonomous system prompt does not reliably stay read-only; it will execute and even commit/push if it judges the work real, which this time was lucky (the fix was correct and well-verified) but is not something to rely on. **Changing next cycle:** a background fork intended as read-only should get `isolation: "worktree"` when the task might touch the shared checkout at all, not just a scoping sentence in the prompt; a sentence is not a lock, which is the exact lesson this whole cycle is about, one level up.

**Next:** hold the line, same as every cycle today; nothing is unblocked without Phil clearing one of the 10 open `decision`/`blocked-on-art` issues. Not regenerating the dashboard again: the merge already carries a real, minutes-old reading with actual egress, and this credential-less sandbox regenerating on top of it would add a timestamp bump with no new information, exactly the move the reachable-carry-forward fix exists to make safe but not something to do needlessly. Not sending a push notification: nothing customer-facing changed.

Pushed to main (`8e4566994`, `9ecd31316`). `ops/preflight.py`, `LEARNINGS.md`, `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md`, this entry. No content, price or product touched, no new page; IndexNow not applicable.

**Correcting my own record, not someone else's.** The entry directly below
this one said the backgrounded `preflight.py` run showed "0 FAIL, 0 traceback
through every gate reached" and used that to justify a "dashboard regen
only" cycle. That was written before the run had actually finished; it had
only reached the documented slow `gate_tests` tail, not completed it. Per
`CLAUDE.md` 0.4, a gate that was still running had not passed, and writing
it as if it had is exactly the defect class this repository tracks hardest.

not by a later cycle.

`test_audit_catalog.py: a wrong price next to 'Guest Vanity Counter Pack'
was not reported against its own SKU`. Investigated rather than trusted
either direction. Read the real catalogue directly: `Vanity Counter Pack`
and `Guest Vanity Counter Pack` are both correctly $4, live. Three
standalone reruns of `test_audit_catalog.py` passed clean. A third, solo
`preflight.py` (no other copy of itself running) passed every gate, 0 FAIL.
Root cause: this session had unknowingly run two full `preflight.py`
processes at once (its own, plus one still alive inside an earlier
background fork), the exact concurrent-fixture-collision shape
`test_audit_catalog.py`'s own comments already document and partially
defend against from 2026-09-05 and 2026-09-08. No live defect, no orphaned
fixture, nothing to ship a fix for. Recorded as LRN-0041 (a learning, not a
new gate: a speculative lock change without being able to reproduce the
narrower kill-mid-write window would be a gate that cannot be proven to
fail).

**Changing next cycle:** this session will not run a second full
`preflight.py` while another of its own background copies might still be
executing one, and will rerun a single named failing test file alone
before writing up a `gate_tests` FAIL as real.

person-delivered services excluded), link_graph_report.py 0 orphans,
b9_claims.py --status 0 undiagnosed rooms.

**Roughly a dozen cycles already reached this exact "nothing new" verdict
today** (git log and this file's own head show PM check-ins and operator
cycles at 11:4x through 15:1x all independently confirming the same
exhausted state). Running a thirteenth identical reconfirmation would have
added nothing issue #42 does not already say, so instead went looking for
ground nothing had swept: `ops/cold_read_ledger.py`'s lanes only ever
covered `ops/*.py`, `ops/*.js`, `site/assets/js/*.js` and
`mobile/quest-app/lib/*.js`. `photos/*.py` (4 files, built 2026-10-14/15,
twice independently security-reviewed per PHOTOS-API.md) had never been
read by this mechanism, and a security review hunts for attacker-triggered
gaps, not an ordinary-use correctness bug.

**Found a real defect reading `photos/store.py` directly.**
`add_photo`/`delete_photo`/`save_analysis` did read-modify-write on one
session's `meta.json` with no lock. `ThreadingHTTPServer` gives every
request its own thread, so two overlapping requests on the same session (a
before and an after photo sent back to back is the ordinary case) could
both read the file before either wrote it back; the second write silently
erased the first writer's new photo entry. The `.jpg` itself still lands on
disk, orphaned, while the caller who uploaded it was already sent `201`.
Proved directly against the pre-fix code with a forced, deterministic
interleave rather than timing luck: both uploads returned `201`, only one
id survived in the listing afterward.

**Fixed.** One re-entrant lock per session (`Store._lock_for`, created only
once a session directory is confirmed to exist, so a flood of guessed or
invalid session ids cannot grow the lock table unboundedly) and a new
`_authorize()` helper (read + token check, no write) let `open()`,
`add_photo`, `delete_photo`, `save_analysis` and `delete_session` each run
their full read-through-write as one locked critical section. Re-proved
fail-then-pass in `ops/tests/test_photos_service.py` (33 to 37 checks): the
new cases force a second request to actually block mid-`open()` while the
first still holds the lock, then confirm both uploads survive.

**Turned the lesson into a gate, not just a fix.** Added `photos/*.py` as a
fifth lane in `ops/cold_read_ledger.py` and ledgered all four files
(`store.py` fixed, the other three clean), so this is a one-time gap, not a
recurring one. `PHOTOS-API.md` and `OWNER-ACTIONS.md` item 22 updated to
the new 37-check count; `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` section 14 records the full
account.

**Verified after:** `test_photos_service.py` 37/37, `test_build_photo_
check_data.py` 5/5, `test_cold_read_ledger_stale.py` 7/7, `test_gate_cold_
read_handoff_not_stale.py` 26/26, `check_urls.py` 213/213, `audit_pages.py`
clean, `fix_dashes.py --check` 0/0, `affiliate.py --check` 165 documents,
`link_graph_report.py` 0 orphans. No price, product or shipped page
touched; `photos/` is still undeployed (Phil's own call,
`OWNER-ACTIONS.md` item 22), so this fix reaches zero live customers today
and closes the gap before his deploy decision could expose it. IndexNow
not applicable.

**Went well:** not repeating a thirteenth identical full reconfirmation;
checking the cold-read ledger's own lane list against what the repository
actually contains rather than trusting "N of N ledgered" at face value.

**Did not go well:** nothing this cycle; the defect found was pre-existing
and pre-deploy, with zero live impact.

**Changing next cycle:** none for the operating loop; the new lane closes
this specific gap. Worth a standing habit, not a rule: when a directory is
added to the repository, check whether it needs to join an existing sweep
lane rather than assuming existing lanes already cover it.

first. Not re-notifying Phil beyond the existing #42 notification: this
finding is informational (pre-deploy, zero live impact) and already fully
recorded here and in PHOTOS-API.md/OWNER-ACTIONS.md for whenever he reads

## 2026-10-15, scheduled operator cycle (video_cleanalong.py's import-order hazard found and fixed)

**Did:** Unshallowed and fast-forwarded cleanly onto origin/main (which kept moving under the hourly-brief/PM-check-in cadence; re-fetched and fast-forwarded twice more during the cycle). Reconfirmed independently rather than cited: all 10 GitHub issues unchanged (decision/blocked-on-art), 0 open PRs, `ops/cycle_signal.py --check` SAME, `cold_read_ledger.py --stale` 0, production `deploy-verdict.json` current (build `c36cb2794e581473` matches `site/build-id.txt`, 0 `site/**`/Dockerfile commits since its `checked_at`), `inbox_agent.py --apply` ran clean (no mail credential in this sandbox, expected). Chased the one red "Checks" run visible in GitHub Actions (runs #2159-2161, `gate_nightly_log_ordering`) to its job log rather than trusting the 08:4x PM check-in's own claim: confirmed those three ran against pre-fix commits and the real fix (`fae87a97b`) was already in flight: genuinely stale, not newly red, matching the claim.

Found and fixed a real defect instead of re-deriving "nothing to do" again: cold-read of `ops/video_cleanalong.py` (new 2026-10-14, 0 log mentions, the oldest un-ledgered candidate `cold_read_ledger.py --next` names). It forced YouTube wide mode on the shared `video_zone` module by appending `--wide` to `sys.argv` before importing it, relying on `video_zone` reading `sys.argv` only once, at its own import time. Proved directly in a throwaway process: importing `video_zone` narrow first, then `video_cleanalong`, left `vz.WIDE` False and `W,H` at 1080x1920 despite `--wide` sitting in `sys.argv`, because the already-cached module never re-read it; `vz.page()`/`vz.shot()` would then silently render portrait frames that the final `ffmpeg scale=1920:1080` stretches into a distorted 16:9 upload, with no error anywhere. `gate_tests` runs every `test_*.py` as its own subprocess (confirmed in `preflight.py`'s own `gate_tests`, one `_run_bounded` call per file), so this ordering never manifests there today, and nothing yet imports `video_cleanalong` from another module (grepped), so there is no live exploit path, only a latent one for whatever batch script combines it with `video_zone` next.

**Verified:** fixed by setting `vz.WIDE`/`vz.W`/`vz.H` directly on the imported module instead of mutating `sys.argv`, which works regardless of import order and leaves `sys.argv` untouched for every other module in the process. Fail-then-pass proved directly against both mechanisms in the adversarial order (old: WIDE stays False; new: WIDE forced True, argv unchanged). `ops/tests/test_video_cleanalong.py` extended with the two checks that prove it (6 to 8), re-run clean standalone. `python -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` clean on both touched files. Ledgered as fixed in `ops/cold-read-ledger.json` with the full account. Full `preflight.py` re-run after the edit; see this entry's own HANDOFF-FILES line and the commit this lands in for its verdict.

**Went well:** the standing cold-read fallback found a genuine, previously-unflagged, demonstrated defect in a brand-new file on the very first candidate, the same shape as the last two cycles' own finds (`rotate_nightly_log.py`, `cycle_signal.py`).

**Changing next cycle:** none; the standing fallback is working as designed.

Three `preflight.py` gates plus STEP 1 of this very prompt each read the whole file on every single run to look at a handful of recent entries, a real and compounding cost (the same shape issue #42 names for the cadence generally, just never traced to this file).

**Fixed:** new `ops/rotate_nightly_log.py` moves entries older than a 14-day window into `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG-ARCHIVE.md`, verbatim, nothing deleted. Date resolution searches each heading for a `YYYY-MM-DD` anywhere in it (about a quarter of entries carry no leading date) and inherits forward from the nearest earlier dated entry otherwise; checked directly against the real file before trusting it (137 of 2,795 entries would have been mis-dated by one day using a leading-only match). Applied once this cycle: live log is now 780 entries / 2.24MB (was 2,795 / 8.06MB). New `gate_nightly_log_not_oversized` in `preflight.py` (WARNING, matching its two neighbours) re-fires if it drifts past retention+7 days again, so this cannot silently regrow. Also extended `ops/cold_read_ledger.py`'s `_mention_counts()` to scan the archive too, since otherwise its own ranking signal would have silently gone stale the moment entries left the live file, the exact "source corrected, downstream not updated" shape this repository keeps finding elsewhere.

**Verified:** `ops/tests/test_rotate_nightly_log.py` and `ops/tests/test_gate_nightly_log_not_oversized.py` both fail-then-pass proved (new gate confirmed to actually warn on a real oversized log and stay silent on a clean one). Ran the new gate directly against the real file both before and after rotation (warned before, clean after). `gate_ops_python_syntax`, `gate_ci_path_filter_covers_preflight_inputs`, `gate_checks_excludes_generated_files`, `gate_nightly_log_ordering`, `gate_nightly_log_no_duplicate_entries`, `gate_cold_read_handoff_not_stale` all re-run directly against the rotated file, clean. Existing `ops/tests/test_nightly_log.py` and `ops/tests/test_cold_read_ledger_stale.py` still pass unmodified. A full `preflight.py` run completed clean before this change (every gate passed, 30 standing sandbox-limitation warnings, no real FAIL) and a second full run was started after this change; it was still running in the background past this entry's own write (known to take up to ~600s), so that specific full-suite confirmation is reported as started, not yet complete, rather than claimed.

**One real defect found and fixed, in check_cron_cadence.py.** `check_one()` computes `delivery_mean`/`delivery_max`/`delivery_n`/`delivery_on_time` for `hourly-brief.yml` (a workflow that throttles inside its own script, judged on `ops/last-brief-sent.json`'s real delivery record rather than its cron) and returns them, including in `--json`. No gate in `ops/preflight.py` reads `main()`'s print output (they all call `check_cron_cadence.check()` directly), so this fix carries no gate risk.

**Went well:** actually running the file against live GitHub Actions history (a `gh auth token` is available in this sandbox) rather than stopping at a static read, which is what surfaced the gap between what was computed and what was shown.

Delegated the full read of both backlogs, the roadmap and the last four log entries to a subagent to keep this session's own context light; it reported every row in `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` sections 2 to 6 Done, Phil-gated, or closed, and named the one real recurring pattern: `gate_dashboard_self_description_fresh` getting re-fixed by hand in nearly every cycle that day. Read 9 open GitHub issues directly: unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`. `inbox_agent.py --apply`: no mail credential, same standing gap. `affiliate.py --check`: clean, 165 documents.

**Verified before acting, not assumed from the subagent's report.** Read `ops/ship.py` and `gate_dashboard_self_description_fresh`'s own docstring in full: the gate already exists, already WARNs correctly, and already explains why it does (lag between regeneration and the next commit is routine). The actual gap was that `ops/ship.py` never ran `ops/dashboard.py` itself outside a rebase conflict, so the deck only ever stayed fresh if a caller remembered a separate manual step first. Traced the real commit stream (`git log --oneline -20`, then `actions_list` against `hourly-brief.yml` directly, 1477 runs): that workflow fires on every push to `main` as well as hourly and commits `CHECKIN-LOG.md` etc. unconditionally, with nothing in the job ever touching the deck, making it the dominant source, not any one session's own pushes.

**Fixed both.** `ops/ship.py` now runs `ops/dashboard.py` unconditionally before staging, on every real (non `--check`) call. `.github/workflows/hourly-brief.yml`'s "Commit the check-in record" step now regenerates the deck first (with `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`/`GH_TOKEN` passed so it degrades the same way a credentialed session would, not worse) and commits its three files alongside the check-in record. Left the three other push-triggered auto-commit workflows (`bluesky-drafts.yml`, `social-drafts.yml`, `linkedin-drafts.yml`) untouched this cycle: each wraps its commit in a more fragile rebase-retry loop already built for a different cross-workflow race, and each commits far less often than the hourly one. Full reasoning in `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` section 9.

**Verified:** `python ops/dashboard.py` runs clean standalone (stdlib only). `python ops/ship.py --check` stays read-only (no dashboard regen, just a report). All three existing `ops/tests/test_ship_*.py` files pass against the changed file. `.github/workflows/hourly-brief.yml` parses as valid YAML. `preflight.py` run to completion in the background: 0 FAIL/WARN through all 74 gates up to the documented `gate_tests` sandbox hang, confirmed genuinely stalled (flat CPU time across a 15-second window) before killing it, same as every other cycle today.

**A second real find while checking the first:** before trusting the commit step actually reaches origin, read this job's own comment above it, which claimed in the present tense that no "Hourly check-in record" commit had ever once succeeded (a 403 permission failure found 2026-09-03). Checked rather than cited: `git log --author=github-actions --grep="Hourly check-in record"` shows 520 such commits in history, the most recent 3 minutes old at the time of this cycle. The comment was true the day it was written and stale ever since (the `permissions: contents: write` block right below it already fixed the real bug); it just never got corrected once the fix landed. Corrected it in place rather than leaving a true-sounding, false claim sitting in a file every future cycle reads. This also means today's actual fix (regenerating the deck in that job) has a real, currently-working commit path to verify against on the next scheduled or push-triggered run, not a hypothetical one.

**Went well:** verifying the subagent's claim against the actual gate docstring and the actual commit stream before trusting it; finding the dominant real cause (one workflow, 1477 runs, not "an operator forgot") rather than writing a fourth gate on a problem the existing one already detects correctly; catching the stale 403 comment by checking it rather than citing it.

**Did not go well:** could not watch the actual next hourly-brief.yml run complete from this sandbox to directly confirm the new "Regenerate the command deck" step succeeds in that job's own environment (GH_TOKEN/STRIPE_SECRET_KEY scoping); the commit mechanism itself is proven live, but this one step is unverified until its first real run.

**Changing next cycle:** if `gate_dashboard_self_description_fresh` still fires after this lands, check the three left-untouched social workflows next, in the order given above, before writing a new gate.

**Next:** standing Phil-gated queue (`OWNER-ACTIONS.md`, 9 open decision/blocked-on-art issues), unchanged.

Pushed to main. `ops/ship.py`, `.github/workflows/hourly-brief.yml`, `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md`, `STATUS.md`, command deck. No price, product or site page touched; not customer-facing, IndexNow not applicable.

## 2026-10-13, scheduled operator cycle: found and fixed a live duplicate-email defect across all three distribution-drafting workflows

**Did:** Unshallowed, attached to main, `merge --ff-only` clean (61 commits fast-forwarded, no unrelated-history symptom). Read `GOALS.md`, `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` in full, `ROADMAP-2026-2029.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the last several `NIGHTLY-LOG.md` entries. `ops/cycle_signal.py --check`: SAME against the last clean snapshot, meaning sections 2-6 of the backlog were already exhausted and GitHub's 9 open issues (checked directly) unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`. `ops/inbox_agent.py --apply`: no mail credential. Per that signal's own instruction, GitHub, CI and the scheduled workflows still needed a direct check this cycle rather than a repeated citation.

**The real finding, checked rather than assumed:** `linkedin-drafts.yml` (LinkedIn is this site's largest identified traffic source, per `GOALS.md`) has a push-triggered fallback specifically built to catch a late cron, gated by a once-a-day commit ledger. Its `schedule`/`workflow_dispatch` branch, though, sent unconditionally on the assumption cron fires at most once a day. It does not fire ON TIME once a day: `gate_scheduled_delivery_phase` already measures this same workflow landing 156 minutes past its own promised time. When the delayed schedule run finally executes after the push fallback has already sent for the day, both paths send. Read directly from `git log --grep='LinkedIn drafts: advance rotation'`: 8 of the last 28 days carried 2 or 3 real send commits in one day, including every day from 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-12 straight. `bluesky-drafts.yml` and `social-drafts.yml` (copied from the same template) carry the identical shape and the identical pattern: 8 of 13 and 8 of 28 tracked days respectively. Phil has been receiving 2 to 3 copies of the same morning drafts on most recent days, on every distribution channel this site actively drafts for.

**Fixed:** all three workflows now send unconditionally only for `workflow_dispatch` (a deliberate manual run); `schedule` falls through to the same "already sent today" commit-ledger check `push` already had. Simulated all six gate branches directly in a throwaway shell script before touching the real files (schedule-on-time, schedule-delayed-after-a-push-send is the bug case, push-before-target, push-fallback-empty-ledger, push-fallback-already-sent, manual-dispatch): all six produced the correct `send=yes`/`send=no`. New `gate_schedule_fallback_race` in `ops/preflight.py`, fail-then-pass proved directly (planted the old pattern in a throwaway file, watched it fail by name, confirmed the real fixed files pass) and against `ops/tests/test_gate_schedule_fallback_race.py` (7/7 cases, including the real committed workflows). Wired into `main()` beside its sibling `gate_push_fallback_ledger_honest`.

**Verified:** full `preflight.py` (fast) run to completion, not cited from a prior cycle: every gate passed, 31 warnings, all previously-diagnosed environment-access limits, no new FAIL. `ops/affiliate.py --check` (165 documents) and `ops/fix_dashes.py --check` (0/0) both clean after. YAML syntax and `ast.parse` on the edited files both clean.

**Went well:** the fix was found by actually reading git history instead of trusting that "the schedule always eventually fires" (the exact assumption the 2026-09-30 sibling fix to this same gate step already named as luck, not evidence) — the duplicate-send pattern was sitting in plain sight in three files' own commit logs the whole time.

**Did not go well:** none this cycle; a real, currently-active, multi-day defect on the one channel this business depends on for traffic went unnoticed through roughly 50+ prior cycles that each independently reconfirmed "nothing new unblocked" without checking whether the thing already shipped was behaving honestly.

**Changing next cycle:** the standing cold-read and backlog-exhaustion checks should periodically re-examine ALREADY-SHIPPED, ALREADY-GATED tooling's own git history for behavioural drift, not just whether its code still matches its own gate. A gate proves the code looks right; it does not prove the workflow has been behaving right in production, which this one had not for at least two weeks.

**Next:** same standing Phil-gated queue (9 open issues, `OWNER-ACTIONS.md`'s items), unchanged. The pre-existing `delivery-phase` warning (linkedin-drafts.yml lands ~156 min late) is a separate, lower-stakes issue (timing drift, not duplication) correctly left untouched per the prior PM check-in's own caution about recalibrating a cron value without enough runs to validate it safely.

Pushed to main. `.github/workflows/linkedin-drafts.yml`, `.github/workflows/bluesky-drafts.yml`, `.github/workflows/social-drafts.yml`, `ops/preflight.py`, `ops/tests/test_gate_schedule_fallback_race.py`, `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md`, command deck. No site, price or product page touched; IndexNow not applicable.

## 2026-10-12, scheduled operator cycle: took the cold-read handoff, found and fixed two real defects in build_image_prompts.py, gated

**Finished?** Yes. Checkout arrived shallow and detached; `git fetch --unshallow`, `checkout main`, `merge --ff-only` onto `origin/main` landed clean, 575 commits, no unrelated-history symptom. `ops/cycle_signal.py --check` reported CHANGED (only `ops/cold-read-ledger.json`, a low-risk bookkeeping row), so ran the real verification rather than skip it. GitHub's 9 open issues unchanged (2 `P0`, rest `decision`/`blocked-on-art`, none mine to pick up per CLAUDE.md 0.5). `ops/inbox_agent.py --apply`: no mail credential, standing. `ops/affiliate.py --check`: clean, 165 documents.

**Took the queued handoff**: second-pass cold read of `build_feed.py`, `build_icons.py`, `build_id.py`, `build_image_prompts.py`, `build_kitchen_deck_pdf.py`. Four read clean (feed regenerates current at 30 entries; icon arc geometry, PNG dimensions and manifest/HTML icon references all check out, cannot execute directly since Pillow is not installed here, standing sandbox limit; build-id hashes git's index deliberately rather than working-tree bytes and matches; kitchen deck PDF's sheet hash matches the live print sheet, and its upstream generator regenerates idempotently).

**The find, in `build_image_prompts.py`, two defects:**

1. `main()`'s `if want_tier:` treated `--tier 0` as no filter at all, because `0` is falsy in Python. The docstring and a long code comment frame tier 0 as "the only number that matters... the whole first batch", so this is exactly the invocation someone would run expecting just the 6-image starter batch; instead it silently wrote all three tier files, 228 prompts. Proved directly: before the fix, `--tier 0` wrote 3 files/228 prompts; after, it writes 1 file/6 prompts. Fixed to `if want_tier is not None:`.

2. The committed `content/images/prompts/tier-1-prompts.md` and `tier-2-prompts.md` were stale against `content.json`'s own text, which had been swept from British to American spelling (`unlabelled`→`unlabeled`, `grey`→`gray`, `labelled`→`labeled`, `tyre`→`tire`, `metre`→`meter`, `Jewellery`→`Jewelry`) but never regenerated afterward. This is the exact "source corrected, shipped artifact never re-derived" shape `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` sections 7 and 8 name as the dominant defect class here. `gate_no_british_spellings_shipped` does not catch it: by design it scopes to `site/**/*.html` and `ops/cardtext/build_*.py`, the things a visitor or Phil-the-card-author actually reads, and these prompt files are an internal image-generation intake queue, never shipped. Regenerated both files from the fixed generator (spelling only; diffed the full change to confirm nothing else moved).

**Fixed and gated:** refactored `build_image_prompts.py`'s `main()` to extract `all_items()`, `render_tier()` and `by_tier()`, so the generator has one source of truth instead of two (the old version duplicated the render logic inline in `main()`, which is what let a defect in it go uncompared against anything). New `gate_image_prompts_tiers_current` in `preflight.py`, mirroring `gate_feed_current`'s regenerate-and-diff pattern, calls those same shared functions and fails if any of the three committed tier files disagrees with a fresh run. Proved fail-then-pass directly (planted the old British spelling back into tier-1, watched the gate fail by name citing the right file, restored, reran clean) and in new `ops/tests/test_gate_image_prompts_tiers_current.py` (5/5 cases, including a missing-file case and a real-corpus-size sanity check). Registered in `main()` next to its sibling `gate_image_prompts_tier0_count_honest`; `GENERATOR_OWNERSHIP` mapping updated to list both gates for `build_image_prompts.py`.

**Verified:** `ops/tests/test_gate_image_prompts_tiers_current.py` 5/5. Direct `--check`/equivalent runs of all five touched/reviewed generators clean (`build_feed.py`, `build_id.py`, `build_kitchen_deck_pdf.py`, plus the new gate itself). `ops/affiliate.py --check` clean. Ran a full `preflight.py --fast` in the background; it was still inside its documented multi-minute `gate_tests` tail when this entry was written, so that tier is reported as **unchecked, not passing**, per CLAUDE.md 0.4, even though every gate directly relevant to this change (the new gate, its sibling, `gate_no_british_spellings_shipped`) was individually exercised and came back clean. Cold-read ledger updated for all five handed-off files, `build_image_prompts.py` marked `fixed` with the full account.

**Went well:** the second-pass cold-read handoff mechanism surfaced two real, previously-invisible defects in a file a first pass had marked clean; both were only visible by actually running the generator's two code paths (`--tier 0` and an unfiltered run) rather than reading the source and trusting the prior note.

**Changing next cycle:** none; the handoff mechanism and the new gate are both working as designed.

Four read clean. **The find, in `build_epub.py`:** `EDITION_DATE`, the hand-maintained constant for the EPUB's `dcterms:modified`, had been `"2026-09-11"` since it was introduced that day and never bumped, despite six real content commits landing in `content/book/` through 2026-10-01 (British-spelling fixes, a `book.css` dedupe, and the chapter 44-49 wrong-room mislabel fix). A fresh regenerate-and-diff of `build/6S-Success-Home-Edition.epub` against the committed file was byte-identical (no build drift; `gate_generator_ownership` already covers that), so the only defect was the date itself silently understating the book's own last real change by three weeks to any retailer reading it.

**Fixed:** bumped to `2026-10-02`, not `2026-10-01`. The newest of those six commits is dated 2026-10-01 in the committer's own local Denver time (-06:00) but 2026-10-02T03:24:01Z in UTC, and the constant is written as an explicit Z-suffixed instant, so the UTC date is the correct one. Rebuilt; the only byte difference anywhere in the unzipped EPUB is the one `dcterms:modified` line.

**Gated it**, per step 10b: new `gate_epub_edition_date_current` in `ops/preflight.py`, compares the constant against `content/book/`'s own latest commit by UTC calendar date (not mtime, not a bare epoch comparison, which a first draft of this gate got wrong against the exact local/UTC day-boundary case that caused the original bug). Proved it can fail: reverted the constant to the stale value by hand, confirmed the gate turns red, restored the fix, confirmed it goes clean again. Registered in `main()` next to its sibling `gate_cover_author_current`, same shape.

**Verified:** both edited files parse clean (`ast.parse`). Ledger updated for all five handed-off files with today's date. `ops/dashboard.py` regenerated (revenue/traffic carried forward, nothing new to report there). Did not re-run the full, slow `gate_tests` tier a second time after this edit: the change is isolated to one non-site Python file plus the one generated artifact it protects, already verified directly against the real function and a real before/after rebuild, which is honest if narrower than a second full suite run.

**Went well:** the handoff mechanism surfaced a real defect a prior second-pass read had marked clean, the exact "stale findings" risk CLAUDE.md 5d warns about, caught here by actually running the generator and diffing rather than re-reading the source and trusting the old ledger note. The gate's first draft (plain epoch comparison) would have been wrong in a way that happened to still fail today for the right reason but for a subtly incorrect one; caught before committing by checking the exact commit timestamp rather than assuming `git log --date=short`'s local-time display was the whole story.

**Did:** Attached clean (fetch, unshallow, checkout main, ff-only onto origin/main). `cycle_signal.py --check`: SAME against the 11:43:36Z snapshot, so skipped the full local re-verification per `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` section 8 and spent the cycle on what signal cannot cover. GitHub read directly: 9 open issues unchanged (all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`), 0 PRs. `inbox_agent.py --apply`: no mail credential, reported unchecked. `list_triggers`: all three Routines healthy, none `FAILED` (this session is the hourly operator's own run). `preflight.py --fast`: 0 FAIL lines through every gate reached, stopped at the documented `gate_tests` sandbox hang. Cold-read ledger: 198/198, 0 stale, 0 un-ledgered candidates, fully exhausted both passes; picked up the most recent PM handoff's own unclaimed work instead, the third-pass adversarial re-read of eight named files.

**The find.** Read `ops/service_orders.py` (forwards paid Virtual Home Consult/In-Home Reset Day/Corporate Lean 6S bookings to Phil with a calendar invite) end to end. `find_time()`'s two `DATE_PATTERNS` are not symmetric: the month-first branch already tolerates a trailing ordinal suffix via its own `\w*` ("Oct. 14th, 2pm" is in the existing test suite and passes), but the day-first branch requires whitespace immediately after the bare day number, so "14th October at 2pm" or "the 14th of October at 2pm" matched nothing and fell through to "no time could be read from the message, so no invite is attached." Same date, two word orders, one worked and one silently didn't, on the highest-value transactions this business has ($250/$1200/enquiry). Confirmed with a standalone regex test against both patterns before touching the file, not assumed from reading alone.

**Fixed:** added an optional `(?:st|nd|rd|th)?,?` after the day-first branch's day capture and an optional `(?:of\s+)?` before the month, mirroring the leniency the month-first branch already had. Verified the existing year-guard regression tests (`"Oct 14, 2027 at 2pm"` etc., the reason this file's bare-digit captures are wrapped in `(?<!\d)...(?!\d)` at all) still correctly return None, and the ambiguous/relative-date cases still correctly return None. Added 2 new cases to `test_service_orders.py` ("14th October at 2pm", "the 14th of October at 2pm"); proved fail-then-pass directly (stashed the fix, watched both new cases fail with the exact right message, restored, reran clean). Full suite: 19 cases, PASS. Recorded in `ops/cold-read-ledger.json` as fixed, with the full account.

**Verified:** `preflight.py --fast` clean (0 FAIL through every gate reached) before and after. No price, product or generated page touched; this is pure Python logic in a hand-maintained ops tool, not something any `ops/build_*.py` owns.

**Went well:** picking up the exact unclaimed handoff from the most recent log entry instead of starting a fresh search; the asymmetry was confirmed with an isolated regex test before editing, not assumed from reading the code.

**Did not go well:** this sandbox still cannot reach Stripe or the live inbox, so whether this bug has ever actually cost a real booking is unknown; `service_orders.py`'s own state file would show it if a real customer email matching this shape had come in and been silently dropped, but reading that requires a session with the IMAP/Stripe credentials this one does not have.

**Changing next cycle:** none; a regression test now covers this shape and would fail the next time the pattern drifts.

**Next:** same standing Phil-gated queue, unchanged (`OWNER-ACTIONS.md` "Start here", the 9 open `decision`/`blocked-on-art` GitHub issues). ## 2026-10-12, scheduled operator cycle: fixed two real indexation_check.py misclassification bugs, PM handoff

**Did:** Attached clean (fetch, unshallow, ff-only onto origin/main, re-synced once more mid-cycle onto a concurrent PM check-in's push, 511 commits). That PM check-in's own handoff named the work: cold-read `ops/indexation_check.py`, the lowest-mention file tied to a live, unresolved priority question (GOALS.md O1: has any individual zone page ever been confirmed indexed).

**Read the file end to end rather than trust its own docstring's "HOW IT REFUSES TO LIE" section, then checked its actual committed output against it.** Two real defects, both confirmed against the live `ops/indexation.json` on disk, not guessed:

1. `classify()` matched `/zones/` and `/articles/` (the sitemap's own hub/listing pages for those sections) by the same substring rule as an individual zone or article page. The ledger's only "zone" entry, ever, was `https://6s-success.com/zones/` itself: the listing page, not a diagnostic zone page. `ops/INDEXATION.md` read "zone: 1" and named `/zones/` under "Zone pages confirmed indexed at least once", stating the exact opposite of the true, still-open answer this file exists to give. Same shape hit `/articles/`.

2. `_domain_urls()` kept any URL containing our domain as a text substring anywhere, not just URLs actually hosted on it. `http://www.bing.com:80/search?q=site%3a6s-success.com`, Bing's own link to its own search-results page carrying our query string, was sitting in "confirmed" permanently, and being additive-only, would have stood as a future trusted canary: a later run could have "proven" it was not blocked by reproducing Bing's own search box link to itself.

**Fixed both at the root.** `classify()` now special-cases the three index-page spellings per section before the substring check, returning "other" (the same bucket the home page's own listing role already gets). Added `_is_our_host()`, checking the actual parsed netloc against the domain (exact or subdomain), and both `_domain_urls()` regex passes now require it before keeping a candidate URL. Added 2 new test cases to `ops/tests/test_indexation_check.py` for each bug; proved both would have caught the regression by stashing the fix and re-running (AttributeError / real failure), then restored it. Re-ran the ledger's own `classify()` over every already-committed URL and dropped the one non-our-host entry; `ops/INDEXATION.md` now correctly reads "zone: 0" and states plainly, in the tool's own designed fallback language, that no individual zone page has ever been confirmed indexed, which is the true, still-open state of GOALS.md O1.

**Verified:** `test_indexation_check.py` and `test_gate_indexation_check_not_stale.py` both pass (the staleness gate is untouched by this fix, confirmed by reading it, since it only checks `checked_at` age). `--dry-run` and `--status` both still behave correctly against the corrected classify(). `check_urls.py` (211/211), `audit_pages.py` (215/0), `fix_dashes.py --check` (0/0). Checked `ops/preflight.py` and `ops/dashboard.py` for any other reader of indexation.json's section counts that might assert a value my fix changes: only `gate_indexation_check_not_stale`, which checks staleness alone, not counts. `GOALS.md`'s own O1 narrative already said "no zone page appeared... suggestive and not evidence", so it was not citing the wrong figure and needed no correction.

**Verified independently rather than inherited, same as every cycle today:** GitHub read directly (9 open issues unchanged, all decision/blocked-on-art, 0 PRs). Network egress re-tested with curl against Stripe, the live site and google.com: all three still rejected by the sandbox proxy (organization policy), consistent with every recent cycle.

**The previous cycle's own claim was NOT finished, and this cycle's real work was finding that out rather than trusting it.** The last several cycles' commit messages and log entries have described `preflight.py` hitting "the already-documented gate_tests sandbox hang" and treated it as environmental, not a defect. Checked this directly against GitHub rather than citing it: the most recent GitHub Actions `Checks` run that actually executed (run #2044, commit `191f0e468`, the one right before the prior cycle's own HEAD) has `conclusion: failure`, not a hang. Its own log shows exactly two real gate failures, both about this same file: `test_gate_nightly_log_ordering.py` and `test_nightly_log.py` both failed because `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md` entry #1889 (dated 2026-10-12) sat after the entry sequence had already moved on to 2026-09-04, i.e. a cycle appended instead of prepending five weeks ago when the stale-log gap was first discovered, and the whole misplaced five-entry block never got moved. Confirmed the defect was still live on the current committed file by running `ops/tests/test_gate_nightly_log_ordering.py` directly (not just importing the gate function, which swallows the failure into a list rather than raising).

**Fixed:** relocated the misplaced five-entry 2026-10-12 block (originally appended after the last 2026-09-04 entry) to sit contiguously at the end of the correctly-ordered 2026-10-12 block already at the top of the file, immediately before the 2026-10-11 entries begin. Verified: `python ops/tests/test_gate_nightly_log_ordering.py` now reports `OK: gate_nightly_log_ordering, 5/5 checks pass`; `python ops/tests/test_nightly_log.py` reports `OK: ops/nightly_log.py, 10/10 checks pass`; `gate_nightly_log_no_duplicate_entries` raises nothing. These were the only two real `FAIL` lines in the CI log; everything else there was `warn` (the standing, already-documented credential/sandbox gaps).

This matters because it means the autonomous CI gate on `ops/` changes (`Checks` workflow) has been genuinely red since whenever this landed, while consecutive cycles described the symptom as a benign local timeout and moved on. The latest commit before this one did not re-trigger `Checks` at all (it only touched the three generated/log files `checks.yml`'s own path filter deliberately excludes), so nothing caught the drift between "local preflight hangs" and "CI preflight actually fails for a different, fixable reason" until this cycle read the Actions API directly instead of citing the commit message.

GitHub re-read directly: 9 open issues unchanged, all `decision` or `blocked-on-art`, 0 open PRs. `inbox_agent.py`: no mail credential, unchecked, not assumed empty.

**Went well:** reading the actual CI run conclusion and log instead of trusting a chain of commit messages that had been citing "known gate_tests hang" without checking whether CI's own result was a hang or a real failure.

**Did not go well:** this exact misattribution (treating a real, fixable gate failure as an unfixable environmental hang) seems to have persisted across multiple cycles; nobody had opened the failed CI run itself until now.

**Changing next cycle:** when `preflight.py` hits the gate_tests slow-suite shape locally, check the live GitHub Actions `Checks` run conclusion for the current or most recent triggering commit before describing it as "the known hang, not a new defect." A local timeout and a CI failure are different claims and this cycle is the proof they can diverge.

Before writing it up as a finding, checked the actual cause rather than the symptom (CLAUDE.md 5d): a `preflight.py` run I had started in the background was still writing to `site/**/*.html` while I ran the generators in the foreground, racing the same files. Recorded the real lesson in the `build_workshop_deck_page.py` ledger note so whoever reads it next does not repeat the scare: never run `preflight.py` and a generator against the same tree at the same time.

**Went well:** catching the race before reporting it as a product defect, and writing the actual cause into the ledger rather than a vague "transient, reran clean."

**Did not go well:** running a backgrounded `preflight.py` alongside foreground generator work in the first place; should have known better given this file's own prior entries about concurrent-session collisions (STATUS.md section 0).

**Changing next cycle:** when `preflight.py` needs to run as part of verifying generator output, run it to completion first or last, never alongside the thing being verified.

## 2026-10-10, scheduled operator cycle, correction (a preflight gate_tests failure this cycle was a race with concurrent git surgery, not a real regression)

**Correcting a scare from this same cycle, written before it could mislead a later one.** After pushing the nightly_log.py atomic-write fix (fd9d954fe), ran a second full `preflight.py` in the background to confirm the final state, but kept working the git merge (checkout, rebase --continue) on the same tree while it ran. That run reported `1 gate(s) failed`: `gate_tests` named `test_gate_affiliate_trigger_citation_current.py` failing with `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError`.

**Verified before believing it.** Ran that one test file standalone against the settled, pushed tree: `OK: gate_affiliate_trigger_citation_current, 5/5 checks pass`. Ran a third full `preflight.py`, this time touching nothing else while it ran: `every gate passed, 29 warning(s)`, clean.

**The lesson:** a backgrounded preflight run reads real files from the working tree as it goes; running `git checkout`/`rebase --continue` concurrently on the same tree can catch a JSON file mid-rewrite and report a false test failure that looks exactly like a real regression. Per CLAUDE.md 0.4, this is recorded rather than quietly dropped, so a future cycle that sees this same test named in a failure does not skip re-verifying it standalone first. No gate needed: the fix is procedural (do not run git surgery and a backgrounded preflight against the same tree at once), not a code defect, and this is a first occurrence, not a recurring pattern.

No files changed by this entry beyond itself and the command deck.

**Cold-read finding, fixed:** the tool's main() wrote NIGHTLY-LOG.md by opening it directly in "w" mode, which truncates the file before the new content is written. A crash mid-write (disk full, kill, container eviction) between truncation and completion would have corrupted the one file this operating prompt calls the only reliable account of what has been tried, the exact failure mode this tool exists to prevent for a different defect class. Fixed with a write-to-temp-file-then-os.replace atomic rename, so the real path is only ever replaced by a fully-written file.

**Proved the fix and the test, not just asserted them.** Added two cases to ops/tests/test_nightly_log.py (5/5 to 7/7): one exercises main() end to end against a real file; the other monkeypatches io.open to fail the temp-file write (simulating disk full) and asserts the real log file comes out byte-identical to before, with no stray .tmp left. Confirmed the new test is not theatre by reverting the atomic-write fix, watching it fail with the exact defect it describes ("real log file changed even though the write failed before the rename"), then restoring the fix and watching it pass again, 7/7.

**Went well:** the cold-read ledger surfaced real, fresh, un-exhausted work instead of another "nothing unblocked" conclusion; the fix was proven against its own regression rather than assumed correct from reading the diff.

The sub-agent found 3 live cases (leave/say/read); independently re-verified by extracting every ACTION CARD step's opening word across all 20 decks and found the real gap is far larger: 108 genuine imperative verbs missing, not 3. Checked each candidate word's actual sentence for mood before adding it (a hazard-list fragment like "Blades. Every blade sheathed..." opens with a noun, not a command, and was excluded), and checked the full candidate set against every real victory text that exists: all 289 ACTION CARD `victory_condition`s across all 20 decks, plus all 114 live `first_15.victory` fields. One word, "dry", had to stay excluded even though it is a genuine imperative elsewhere in the corpus ("Dry the vanity counter...") because this file's own founding example, "Dry basin, two tools standing, nothing lying in water," uses the identical word as a state adjective, and that sentence is the one this file was written to keep passing. Fixed: rebuilt the set (56 to 162 words) and the docstring. New cases 10-11 in `ops/tests/test_diagnosis_schema.py` (the 3-word regression plus all 289 cross-deck victories), fail-then-pass proved against the reverted set. All 5 existing diagnosis test files rerun clean after.

2. **`ops/deploy_freshness.py`'s own comment claimed its 4 discovery pages "reference every fingerprinted asset the site ships." False: `site/downloads/assets/book.css` (written by `ops/build_sample_html.py`, fingerprinted by `ops/fingerprint_assets.py`) is referenced only by the downloads/ sample page, which was not in the list, so it was never compared to production at all.** Independently re-verified and found the bug was worse than "a missing list entry": the referencing page's own href is `assets/book.css`, relative to ITS OWN directory (`site/downloads/`), not to `site/` root like every page already in the list, so simply adding the page would not have been enough. `ops/preflight.py`'s sibling gate (`gate_checker_scope`, meant to catch exactly "an asset no discovery page covers") also could not have caught this, independently confirmed by running it directly: it builds its "shipped" set from `all_pages()`, which deliberately excludes `downloads/` for unrelated reasons (dash/claim gates should not scan the book sample's hand-written prose), so `assets/book.css` was never even in its shipped set to begin with; and even if it had been, the gate's own existence check joined the match straight onto `SITE` (`site/assets/book.css`, which does not exist) instead of resolving it against the referencing page's directory. Fixed: added `resolve_asset_ref()` to `deploy_freshness.py` (resolves an href against the page it was found on, the way a browser does) and the missing discovery page; `gate_checker_scope` now imports and shares the same resolver instead of its own drifted copy, and explicitly scans `downloads/*.html` for its "shipped" set alongside `all_pages()`. Fail-then-pass proved three ways: `test_deploy_freshness.py` (4 resolver cases plus an end-to-end book.css comparison, 12 of 12 passing; raises `AttributeError` against the reverted file, confirming the function did not exist before), `test_gates.py` (new `checker-scope` case, plants a downloads/ page plus its asset, fails on the reverted `preflight.py`, passes on the fix), and `gate_checker_scope()` called directly before/after. The actual divergence this surfaced between `content/book/assets/book.css` and `site/downloads/assets/book.css` (8 lines) is not a bug: `ops/build_sample_html.py` deliberately adds a `.figalt` rule to the shipped copy that the book source does not carry, confirmed by reading that generator directly before treating the diff as a finding.

## 2026-10-09, scheduled operator cycle, addendum: a delegated CI check caught a real, currently-live blocker the first pass of that same check had cleared by mistake

**What happened.** After pushing the cold-read commit above, a delegated sub-agent checking CI status first reported (wrongly) that `publish-image.yml`'s prior FAIL (run #589, commit `170f13d1`, `gate_generator_ownership` failing on `site/sitemap.xml`) was already fixed by later commits, based on running one generator (`ops/build_resources.py`) standalone and seeing byte-identical output. That was a false negative: the gate's own docstring explains why running one generator alone cannot reproduce this class of drift (lastmod/content-hash state depends on the whole 43-generator chain running in order). The same sub-agent then ran the real full chain in the background, caught its own error, and sent a correction: the FAIL was still live at HEAD.

**Fixed.** Ran the real `GENERATOR_OWNERSHIP_CHAIN` directly (43 generators, skipping `build_zone_pages.py`/`build_epub.py` per the gate's own documented sandbox exclusions, no local hero photos or book images here), for real rather than through the gate's own checkout-and-restore wrapper, to see and keep the actual diff. One file changed: `site/sitemap.xml`, 212 URLs to 211. The committed sitemap carried a stray, malformed duplicate `<url>` block for `https://6s-success.com/rooms/laundry-room` (wrong position in the file, lastmod `2026-10-09`, no `image:image` block) alongside the real, correct one (lastmod `2026-10-02`, image block present). Traced to commit `a40c4d2a` (this session's own earlier cold-read fix today), which ran `ops/build_seo.py` standalone to refresh lastmod on 114 changed pages; only one physical file now carries that canonical URL, so this reads as a transient race with a concurrent session's write at the moment that standalone run scanned the tree, not a reproducible logic bug in `build_seo.py` itself (no second source file exists to explain a deterministic duplicate). `ops/build_id.py` rerun (pre-commit hook caught the resulting staleness correctly, exactly as designed).

**Verified:** `check_urls.py` 211/211, `audit_pages.py` 215/0, `fix_dashes.py --check` clean, `affiliate.py --check` clean (165 documents). A background `preflight.py --own` run against the clean, committed tree is this fix's own authoritative confirmation; also triggers a real `publish-image.yml` run (this commit touches `site/**`), which is the actual test that matters.

**Went well:** the sub-agent self-corrected its own false negative within the same investigation rather than letting a wrong "already fixed" stand; delegating CI-status checks surfaced a real, live blocker this cycle's own earlier work had accidentally introduced, closing the loop within the same session rather than leaving it for the next cycle to rediscover.

**Did not go well:** running one generator in isolation to "confirm" a chain-wide gate is a trap worth naming for next time: `gate_generator_ownership`'s own docstring already says not to run `build_seo.py` standalone for exactly this reason, and the first check still did the equivalent (checked one piece of the chain and generalized to the whole chain).

**Changing next cycle:** none; the existing gate caught the original defect correctly. Worth remembering: a generator-ownership verification is only real if the full chain runs, not a sampled piece of it.

Pushed to main (`48a4c07c4`). `site/sitemap.xml`, `site/build-id.txt`. No price or product touched, no new page; the one page's lastmod correction is a dedup, not new content, so IndexNow is not applicable.
